text:
Arrange the following amines in the decreasing order of basicity : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

Basic nature depends on the tendency of donating the lone pair. 

In (I) st amine lone pair of N atom is not in resonance. So it can easily donate the lone pair. 

In (II) amine lone pair of N atom is in resonance. So, lone pair is not available. 

In (III) amine lone pair of N atom is not in resonance so lone pair can be easily donated. 

So, (I) and (III) are more basic compared to (II). 

In (I) amine N atom is connected to $sp^{2}$ hybridised carbon atom and in (III)  amine N atom is connected to $sp^{3}$ hybridised carbon atom. 

We know $sp^{2}$ carbon atom  has more $-$ I effect than $sp^{3}$ carbon atom. 

So, in  (I) amine density  of electrons around N atom will decrease due to $-$ I effect and basic nature also decrease.

So, correct order of basic nature  :  III > I > II
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text: Aluminium is usually found in +3 oxidation state. In contrast, thallium exists in + 1 and + 3 oxidation states. This is due to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Electronic configuration of Thallium (Tl) is 

= [Xe]$4f^{14} 5d^{10} 6s^{2} 6p^{1}$

Here because of poor sheilding of 4f and 5d orbital on 6s orbital, electrons of 6s orbital is more tightly held by the nucleus and perticipate less in bond formation. This is called as innert pair effect. And that is why Tl become stable in +1 oxidation state.

text: In general, the properties that decrease and increase down a group in the periodic table, respectively, are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Electronegativity decreases down the group because the increased number of energy levels puts the outer electrons very far away from the pull of nucleus. 

Atomic radius increases down the group because the number of energy levels increases when you move down the group. Each subsequent energy level is further from the nucleus than the last. That is why atomic radius increases down the group.

text: The highest value of the calculated spin only  magnetic moment  (in BM) among all the transition metal complexes is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The spin-only moment $μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM increases with the number of unpaired electrons $n$.

In a complex the valence electrons of the metal are all in the 3d orbitals: the 4s electrons are lost first on ionisation, and the 4s and 4p orbitals receive the ligand electron pairs. The five 3d orbitals hold at most 5 unpaired electrons, in high-spin $d^{5}$ complexes such as $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{3+}$.

The 6 unpaired electrons of the free Cr atom ($3d^{5}4s^{1}$) do not occur in a complex; even Cr(0) in $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{6}]$ is $3d^{6}$.

$μ_{\max }=\sqrt{5(5+2)}=\sqrt{35}=5.92\text{BM}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following is true with respect to $Li_{2}^{+}$ and $Li_{2}^{-}$ ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$Li_{2}^{+}$  (5 electrons) = $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{1}}$

$Li_{2}^{-}$  (7 electrons) = $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}$  $σ_{2s^{1}}^{\ast }$

$\therefore$   Bond order of $Li_{2}^{+}$  = $\frac{3-2}{2}$ = 0.5

Bond order of $Li_{2}^{-}$ = $\frac{4-3}{2}$ = 0.5

As both  $Li_{2}^{+}$ and $Li_{2}^{-}$ has non-zero bond order, so both are stable.

text: Two complexes [$Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$Cl_{3} (A)$ and [$Cr(NH_{3})_{6}$]$Cl_{3} (B)$ are violet and yellow coloured, respectively. The incorrect statement regarding them is :
options: $\Delta_{0}$ values of (A) and (B) are calculated from the energies of violet and yellow light, respectively
both are paramagnetic with three unpaired electrons
both absorb energies corresponding to their complementary colors.
$\Delta_{0}$ value for (A) is less than that of (B).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Both complexes contain $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{3}$, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{0}$), so both are paramagnetic with three unpaired electrons: statement (B) is correct.

The colour seen is complementary to the colour absorbed, so violet complex (A) absorbs yellow light and yellow complex (B) absorbs violet light: statement (C) is correct.

$\Delta _{o}$ equals the energy of the light absorbed, $\Delta _{o}=\dfrac{hc}{λ_{\text{absorbed}}}$, so $\Delta _{o}$ of (A) is obtained from yellow light and that of (B) from violet light, not the other way round: statement (A) is incorrect.

$\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is a stronger field ligand than $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, consistent with (B) absorbing higher-energy violet light, so $\Delta _{o}$ of (A) is less than that of (B): statement (D) is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text: 20 mL of $0.1 M H_{2}SO_{4}$ solution is added to 30 mL of $0.2 M NH_{4}OH$ solution. The pH of the resultant mixture is : [$pK_{b}$ of $NH_{4}OH = 4.7$].
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Millimoles taken: $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}=20\times 0.1=2$ and $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}=30\times 0.2=6$.

$\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}+2\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

2 mmol $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ consumes 4 mmol $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ and gives 2 mmol $(\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$, that is, 4 mmol $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}$. The $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ left is $6-4=2$ mmol.

The solution contains $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ and its conjugate acid $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}$, a basic buffer. Both are in the same volume, so the ratio of millimoles can be used:

$\text{pOH}=\text{p}K_{b}+\log \frac{[\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}{}^{+}]}{[\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}]}=4.7+\log \frac{4}{2}=4.7+0.3=5.0$

$\text{pH}=14-5.0=9.0$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
The following results were obtained during kinetic studies of the reaction ; 

2A + B $\to$ Products

  
    Experiment
    [A] (in mol $L^{-1})$
    [B] (in mol $L^{-1})$
    Initial Rate of reaction
(In mol $L^{-1} \min ^{-1})$
  
  
    I
    0.10
    0.20
    $6.93 × 10^{-3}$
  
  
    II
    0.10
    0.25
    $6.93 × 10^{-3}$
  
  
    III
    0.20
    0.30
    $1.386 × 10^{-2}$
  

The time (in minutes) required to consume half of A is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Experiments I and II: raising $[\mathrm{B}]$ from $0.20$ to $0.25\text{mol L}^{-1}$ leaves the rate unchanged, so the reaction is zero order in B.

Experiments I and III: doubling $[\mathrm{A}]$ doubles the rate, so the reaction is first order in A and $\text{rate}=k[\mathrm{A}]$.

From experiment I, $k=\dfrac{6.93\times 10^{-3}}{0.10}=6.93\times 10^{-2}\text{\min }^{-1}$.

For $2\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}\to \mathrm{Products}$, $\text{rate}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{A}]}{dt}$, so $-\dfrac{d[\mathrm{A}]}{dt}=2k[\mathrm{A}]$.

$t_{1/2}=\dfrac{0.693}{2k}=\dfrac{0.693}{2\times 6.93\times 10^{-2}}=5\text{\min }$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text: Which one of the following statements regarding  Henry's law is not correct ?
options: Higher the value of $K_{H}$ at a given pressure, higher is the solubility of the gas in the liquids
Different gases have different $K_{H} ($Henry's law constant) values at the same temperature.
The partial pressure of the gas in vapour phase is proportional to the mole fraction of the gas in the solution.
The value of $K_{H}$ increases with increase of temperature and $K_{H}$ is function of the nature of the gas
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From Henry's law we know, 

$P_{$gas$} = K_{H} x_{g}$

Where, Pgas = Pressure of undissolved gas 

$x_{g} =$ Mole fraction of gas dissolved into  the liquid. 

$K_{H} =$ Henry's constant. 

When pressure is constant then,

$x_{g}$ $\propto$ $\frac{1}{K{}_{H}}$

So, when $K_{H}$ is high then $x_{g}$ or solubility of gas is lower in the liquid.

So, option (A) is wrong.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text: Consider the reversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas in a closed system at two different temperatures $T_{1}$ and $T_{2} (T_{1} < T_{2})$. The correct graphical depiction of the dependence of work done (w) on the final volume (V) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a reversible isothermal expansion of $n$ mol of an ideal gas from initial volume $V_{1}$ to final volume $V$:

$w=-nRT\ln \dfrac{V}{V_{1}}\Rightarrow |w|=nRT\ln V-nRT\ln V_{1}$

So $|w|$ against $\ln V$ is a straight line of slope $nRT$ that meets the $\ln V$ axis, where $|w|=0$, at $\ln V=\ln V_{1}$, the start of the expansion.

For the same gas sample expanding from the same initial volume at $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$, both lines start from the same point on the $\ln V$ axis; since $T_{2}>T_{1}$, the $T_{2}$ line is steeper and lies above the $T_{1}$ line at every $V>V_{1}$, so the lines do not cross.

Graph (C) shows this; the lines in (A) and (B) cross, and those in (D) start with non-zero work.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot
